fields.h1: Build a Health Coaching Intake Form That Measures Readiness
fields.hero_description: Build a health coaching intake form that rates each client's readiness to change and puts the scores on the coach's prep sheet.
fields.features_heading: What a Coach Knows Before the First Call
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds a health coaching intake form around the habit a client wants to change and the history a coach should know.
fields.feature_1:
Importance and confidence, rated apart

Ask the client to name one habit, then rate how important it is and how confident they feel about it, each from 1 to 10. Both scores sit side by side on the coach's prep sheet.
fields.feature_2:
Sections for the areas a client picks

A client who picks sleep sees questions on bedtime and coffee, and one who picks stress gets questions on workload. Nobody scrolls past a section that does not apply to them.
fields.feature_3:
A question about care already under way

Ask whether a doctor is treating any condition and, if so, for the doctor's name. The coach knows who else is involved before agreeing on a goal that touches food or exercise.
fields.feature_4:
A coaching agreement signed on the form

Close the intake with your coaching agreement, session terms included, and a typed or drawn signature. Each signature is saved with its date next to the answers that came with it.
fields.feature_5:
An email or Slack alert for each new intake

Every submitted intake sends the coach an email or a Slack message with the client's name and the habit they chose. The full answers wait on the prep sheet before the first call.
fields.feature_6:
Code that moves to your own GitHub

On paid plans, export the code for the intake and the prep sheet to your GitHub repository. A developer can then host it on your own servers and keep building on it from there.

faq_plan.q: What is a health coaching intake form?
How do I create a health coaching intake form?

plan.angle: Searches for a health coaching intake form return printable questionnaires that list every lifestyle topic and stop there. This page shows the questions that set the first coaching goal, readiness to change above all, and four coaching practices whose online intake acts on the answers: a virtual practice that opens on a confidence gap, an employer program that assigns coaches by focus area, a sleep coach who gets hours slept worked out, and weekly check-ins that alert the coach when a client goes quiet.
tab_stories: Rafael Ostrowski rates walking after dinner 9 for importance and 4 for confidence on Fernhollow Health Coaching's intake, and Corinne Abernathy opens his first video call on the 5-point gap.
Brackenridge Freight employees enroll in Tidewater Coaching Group's program by picking one focus area, each area goes to its own coach, and HR sees 46 enrollments by area with no answers attached.
Theo Marchetti enters a 12:30 bedtime and a 6:15 wake time on Wrenfield Sleep Coaching's intake, and Imogen Achterberg sees 5 hours 45 minutes beside his 2 coffees after 2 pm.
Noor Halvorsen skips Larkspur Health Coaching's Sunday check-in on Oct 18 and Oct 25, and Benedikt Varga gets an email on Monday with her last stress score.
